baseline: Host Linux 6.8.0 with LTP 20260529: brk02 passes 2/2 (both libc and syscall variants). The test expands the heap by 2 pages, calls mprotect(middle_page, PROT_READ) to split the heap into multiple VMAs, then expands by one more page and shrinks back to the original break. All operations succeed. Empirical observation via /proc/self/maps: after mprotect, heap consists of [B-2p,B-p) rw + [B-p,B) r--; after the post-mprotect expand to B+p, a new VMA [B,B+p) rw-p is created (not an extension of the read-only VMA), and writing to the new page succeeds. The brk syscall returns exactly the requested break at each step.
failing_assertion: brk02.c:75 in both variants: "Cannot expand brk() after mprotect". Libc variant: brk(B0+3*PAGE_SIZE) returns B0+2*PAGE_SIZE (unchanged) instead of B0+3*PAGE_SIZE; glibc's brk() wrapper detects newbrk < requested and returns -1 with ENOMEM, failing both the TST_EXP_PASS_SILENT check at line 25 and the subsequent sbrk(0) != requested check at line 74-76 (2 TFAILs). Syscall variant: tst_syscall(__NR_brk, B0+3*PAGE_SIZE) returns B0+2*PAGE_SIZE, which is < the target, so the comparison at line 74 fails (1 TFAIL). Total: 0 passed, 3 failed. The shrink-back step (line 79) is never reached because the test returns early after the expand failure.
root_cause: Heap::modify_heap_end calls vmar.resize_mapping(heap_start, old_size, new_size, check_single_mapping=true). The check_single_mapping flag invokes VmarInner::check_lies_in_single_mapping (kernel/src/vm/vmar/vmar_impls/mod.rs:211-221), which requires the entire heap range [heap_start, heap_start+old_size) to be covered by a single VmMapping. After mprotect(B0+PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE, PROT_READ), Vmar::protect (vmar_impls/protect.rs:56) splits the heap's single VmMapping into two: [heap_start, B0+PAGE_SIZE) with RW permissions and [B0+PAGE_SIZE, B0+2*PAGE_SIZE) with READ permissions. When brk(B0+3*PAGE_SIZE) is called, check_lies_in_single_mapping(heap_start, old_size=2*PAGE_SIZE) does find_one(&heap_start), which returns the first mapping ending at B0+PAGE_SIZE. The filter checks whether map_end - heap_start >= old_size, i.e., PAGE_SIZE >= 2*PAGE_SIZE, which is false. The function returns Err(EFAULT), resize_mapping propagates the error, and modify_heap_end's .map_err closure returns Err(current_heap_end=B0+2*PAGE_SIZE). sys_brk (kernel/src/syscall/brk.rs:20) catches this with .unwrap_or_else(|cur_heap_end| cur_heap_end) and returns the unchanged break. The comment at heap.rs:138-142 explicitly states that check_single_mapping=true was chosen 'for simplicity', not correctness.
invariant: The program break (as manipulated by brk/sbrk) must be adjustable up or down regardless of how the heap's virtual address range is partitioned into VmMappings. User code may call mprotect, mmap(MAP_FIXED), or munmap within the heap range, fragmenting it into multiple mappings with different permissions or leaving holes. brk must tolerate this fragmentation: expansion creates or extends mappings to cover the new heap end, and shrinking unmaps the released range even if it spans multiple mappings. Newly exposed heap pages must have the default heap permissions (VM_READ | VM_WRITE), not inherit permissions from an adjacent mapping—this ensures writes to malloc'd memory succeed even after the allocator has mprotected part of the heap.
owning_layer: Process heap-management layer (Heap::modify_heap_end in kernel/src/process/process_vm/heap.rs), which translates the abstract 'program break' into VMA operations. This corresponds to Linux's do_brk_flags (mm/vma.c), which sits above the generic VMA layer and enforces heap-specific semantics: it attempts vma_merge_new_range with VM_DATA_DEFAULT_FLAGS, and if merge fails (e.g., due to mismatched permissions), it allocates a fresh VMA with the heap's default RW flags. Asterinas's resize_mapping is a lower-level primitive (equivalent to Linux's vma_expand or direct vma surgery) and does not have brk-specific logic, so the heap layer must either use a different VMAR operation or implement the permission-checking and fresh-mapping-creation itself.
linux_reference: Linux v6.16.9 mm/mmap.c SYSCALL_DEFINE1(brk, ...) lines 120-215: sys_brk computes newbrk = PAGE_ALIGN(brk), and for expansion (brk > mm->brk) calls do_brk_flags(&vmi, brkvma, oldbrk, newbrk - oldbrk, 0) at line 197. For shrinking, it calls do_vmi_align_munmap(&vmi, brkvma, mm, newbrk, oldbrk, &uf, true) at line 180, which unmaps [newbrk, oldbrk) across however many VMAs exist in that range—no single-VMA requirement. do_brk_flags (mm/vma.c:2714-2780) computes flags = VM_DATA_DEFAULT_FLAGS | VM_ACCOUNT | mm->def_flags (line 2724), and if vma && vma->vm_end == addr, attempts vma_merge_new_range(&vmg) to extend the preceding VMA (lines 2738-2747). If merge fails or no preceding VMA, it creates a fresh vm_area_struct with vm_flags_init(vma, flags) (line 2757), ensuring the new region has the default heap permissions. The merge uses is_mergeable_vma which compares vm_flags, so a read-only VMA will not merge with the RW heap extension, triggering fresh VMA creation.
other_callers: Within the brk/sbrk syscall path, modify_heap_end is the sole caller, reached via sys_brk (kernel/src/syscall/brk.rs). The defect affects any process that: (1) uses mprotect to change permissions on part of its heap (e.g., memory allocators creating guard pages, or security-hardening schemes), then (2) calls brk to expand or shrink. It also affects processes that mmap(MAP_FIXED) or munmap within the heap range, fragmenting it. These are not exotic—jemalloc and tcmalloc use mprotect for guards, and some allocators use mmap for large allocations within the heap range. The check_single_mapping=true guard also blocks shrinking when the heap is split: after the mprotect in brk02, if the expand had succeeded, the shrink-back step would also fail for the same reason (the heap spans 3 mappings at that point). Currently this is not exercised because the test returns early. Outside brk, kernel/src/syscall/mremap.rs:109 uses resize_mapping(..., true) for MREMAP_FIXED without MREMAP_MAYMOVE, but that path has user-controlled semantics ("move this exact mapping") where single-mapping is arguably correct, so it is out of scope for this fix.
suggested_direction: Replace the single check_single_mapping=true call with brk-specific logic: (1) For expansion: check whether the last VmMapping in the heap range (find_one at old_heap_end - 1) exists, is expandable (can_expand()), and has the default heap permissions (VmPerms::READ | VmPerms::WRITE). If all conditions hold, enlarge that mapping via VmarInner::resize_mapping with check_single_mapping=false (which already handles the case where the heap is fragmented—line 54 checks that at least one mapping exists at the start). If the last mapping has wrong permissions or doesn't exist (e.g., munmap'd the top page), allocate a fresh VmMapping with heap permissions covering [old_heap_end, new_heap_end). (2) For shrinking: VmarInner::resize_mapping's shrink path (lines 448-459) already calls alloc_free_region_exact_truncate, which iterates over all intersecting mappings and truncates them (lines 322-342), so setting check_single_mapping=false makes shrink work across splits. (3) Guard against edge cases: if find_one(old_heap_end - 1) returns None (heap top was unmapped), treat as "wrong permissions" and allocate fresh. If the new heap size is larger and alloc_free_region_exact fails (something else is mapped where the heap wants to grow), return Err(current_heap_end) as today—this is the correct ENOMEM. (4) Alternatively, implement a dedicated Vmar::resize_heap method encapsulating this logic, keeping resize_mapping's stricter semantics for mremap. The key invariant to test: after any mprotect/mmap/munmap fragmentation, brk up/down must succeed and newly allocated heap pages must be writable (verified by writing to them, as brk01.c:66 does for the non-split case).
